titles.629: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — logicians' definitions mark aptitudo not act (albedo / sight)
titles.630: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — bad tree / bird analogies: infants and unfledged birds still have the nature
titles.631: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Sohnius vs Anabaptists: Hebrew peccare actual and habitual (inherent defect)
titles.632: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — 'we did not sin actu in original sin except as in Adam' — did we sin actu when he did?

latin.629: Eodem sensu Logici notare solent verba in definitionibus posita aptitudinem, non actum designare, ut cum definitur albedo, Color qui visum disgregat, id est, qui aptus natus est visum disgregare.
latin.630: Sic cum Dominus dicit omnem arborem malam malos ferre fructus, male colligeret qui infidelium irregenitos infantulos malas arbores esse negaret, quod non ferant malos fructus; haud secus certe ac qui legisset, omnem volucrem volare, male inde concluderet, aviculam recens exclusam, quod nondum volet, volucrem non esse.
latin.631: Itaque Anabaptistis quibusdam idem quod tu obiicientibus, peccare esse verbum activum & actionem significare, Georgius Sohnius nihil respondit, nisi verba apud Hebraeos non tantum significare actualiter, sed etiam habitualiter; hoc est, non tantum actionem, sed etiam defectum & pravitatem inhaerentem.
latin.632: Caeterum non satis intelligo tua ista verba, In peccato originali non peccavimus actu, nisi quatenus in Adamo peccavimus. Quid enim? Visne nos actu peccavisse in Adamo tum cum peccavit?
latin.633: Id Zanchius, quem tu pro tua sententia laudas Cap. tui tractatus vii. negat, addita hac ratione, quia nondum eramus actu. Nam qui fieri potuit, ut, quum nondum essemus actu, peccaremus actu?
latin.634: Unde sic argumentor: Moriuntur homines actu. Ergo peccaverunt actu. Absurdum enim est ut qui potentia tantum peccavit, non autem actu, puniatur actu, & quidem poena gravissima. Atqui non peccaverunt actu in Adamo cum peccavit actualiter. Aliud igitur sit oportet peccatum ob quod actu moriantur homines, nempe vitium illud originale, quo quod omnibus & singulis inest vere & proprie, actu, inhaerenter; tam certe actu quam fuit in ipso Adamo.

pass_a.629: Placeus backs the Clavis with the logicians: definition-words often name aptitude, not a completed act—as whiteness is 'color that scatters sight,' meaning born apt to do so.
pass_a.630: Same pattern in the Lord's 'bad tree / bad fruit': unregenerate infants are still bad trees though fruitless yet—just as a newly hatched chick is still a bird though it does not yet fly.
pass_a.631: Against Anabaptist (and Garrigues-like) insistence that peccare names only an action, Sohnius answered that Hebrew can mean habitually too—an inherent defect and wickedness, not only the deed.
pass_a.632: Placeus presses Garrigues's line that in original sin we did not sin actu except as in Adam: does that mean we actually sinned in Adam at the moment he sinned?
pass_a.633: Zanchius—whom Garrigues himself cites favorably in ch. 7—denies that: we were not yet actu, so we could not then sin actu. Placeus makes the question sharp against Garrigues's wording.
pass_a.634: Tip argument: men die by act, so they have sinned by act—punishing in act for mere potency is absurd. They did not sin by act in Adam when he actually sinned. So another sin grounds their actual death: the original vice inherent in each and all, truly and properly by act, as certainly as it was in Adam himself. Tip before 'he sinned for all his posterity.'

629: In the same sense logicians usually note that words set in definitions mark an aptitude, not an act—as when whiteness is defined as a color that scatters sight, that is, that is born apt to scatter sight.
630: So when the Lord says every bad tree bears bad fruit, he would gather poorly who denied that the unregenerate infants of unbelievers are bad trees because they do not yet bear bad fruit. No otherwise than if, reading that every bird flies, he concluded that a chick just hatched, because it does not yet fly, is not a bird.
631: And so to certain Anabaptists objecting—as you do—that "to sin" is an active verb and signifies an action, Georgius Sohnius answered nothing except that among the Hebrews words signify not only actually but also habitually. That is, not only an action, but also an inherent defect and wickedness.
632: For the rest I do not well enough understand those words of yours: "In original sin we did not sin by act, except insofar as we sinned in Adam." What then? Do you mean that we sinned by act in Adam at the time when he sinned?
633: That Zanchius—whom you praise for your view in chapter 7 of your treatise—denies, adding this reason: because we were not yet in act. For how could it be that, when we were not yet in act, we should sin by act?
634: From which I argue thus: Men die by act. Therefore they have sinned by act. For it is absurd that one who has sinned only in potency, not in act, should be punished in act—and with a most heavy penalty. And yet they did not sin by act in Adam when he sinned actually. There must therefore be another sin because of which men die by act: namely that original vice which is in all and each truly and properly, by act, inherently—as certainly by act as it was in Adam himself.

633.gloss: we were not yet in act

632.choice: Did we sin actu in Adam when he sinned?
